1) the intradiscal pressure and shear strain are higher in the nucleus pulposus than in the annulus fibrosus under axial compression; 2) the intradical pressure is higher in the nucleus than in the annuls under axial rotation, while the shear strain is higher in the annuls than in the nucleus; and 3) the fiber strain is higher in both the nucleus and the annuls under torsion, and is highest in the annuls fibrosus
(a) the intervertebral discs are subjected to large shear and tensile strains under combined loads, and that (b) the shear strain and the tensile strain are correlated with the intradiscal pressure.
